text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Aspirin with clopidogrel for 21 days after the minor stroke, then clopidogrel 75 mg alone
  • Atorvastatin 80 mg with a lipid panel 4 to 12 weeks after starting, aiming for LDL cholesterol below 70 mg/dL
  • Lower blood pressure below 130/80 with amlodipine and lisinopril, checking standing blood pressure at each visit and a basic metabolic panel 1 to 2 weeks after starting lisinopril
  • Neurology consultation to confirm the stroke mechanism, set the antiplatelet plan after the 21-day course, decide on prolonged cardiac rhythm monitoring, and advise on return to work and public speaking
  • Outpatient physical and occupational therapy for left-sided weakness, with fall-risk review at every visit
  • PHQ-9 at the first visit and at each review while symptoms persist, MoCA again within the first year, and attention to post-stroke tearfulness
  • Brief interventions at every visit for unhealthy alcohol use (AUDIT-C, no more than two drinks a day) and cigar smoking, with nicotine replacement offered
  • Yearly influenza vaccine and current COVID-19 vaccine

resource.title: Winston Churchill synthetic care plan
resource.description: Manage the first three months after a minor right-hemisphere lacunar stroke in a 78-year-old who intends to return to demanding public work: a 21-day dual antiplatelet course then clopidogrel alone, a high-intensity statin, blood pressure lowered to below 130/80 without orthostatic hypotension, prolonged rhythm monitoring for atrial fibrillation, rehabilitation, and measurement-based screening for post-stroke depression, cognitive change, unhealthy alcohol use, and cigar smoking on the CMID stroke schedule.
